newsitem.title: UK: Boeing, M-D announce major airline sales orders.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, M-D announce major airline sales orders.

text.p: Boeing Co. and rival McDonnell Douglas Corp. Monday announced new aircraft sales worth more than $6.6 billion at Britain's Farnborough air show.

Boeing said its orders, worth $6.3 billion, included the launch sale for a bigger version of its 757 twin jet, the 757-300X, which has 20 percent more capacity. The 757 order is from German vacation airline Condor Flugdienst in a deal for 12 aircraft plus 12 options worth about $800 million.
Boeing said the orders also include sales to British Airways, Ansett Worldwide, International Lease Finance Corp., Airtours, Air Berlin, LOT Polish Airlines, Maersk Air and TACA.
Mike Sears, president of the Douglas Aircraft Corp., told reporters that McDonnell Douglas had six firm orders from four airlines for new planes worth $365 million.

Boeing's order from British Airlines is for four 747-400s, three 777-200s and three 757-200s. The British carrier also reconfirmed orders for 10 747-400s, bringing delivery forward to replace older 747-100s.

Australian leasing firm Ansett Worldwide bought 10 737-700s, six 737-300s and nine 767-300 ERs (extended range planes). U.S. leasing giant ILFC acquired 156 aircraft including five 757-200s, five 767-300 ERs and five 737s.
LOT has bought two 737-400s and one 767-300 ER, Danish carrier Maersk has acquired three 737-500s, Air Berlin bought one 737-400 and British holiday firm Airtours one 767-300 ER.

Sears said McDonnell Douglas sold one MD90 and two options to Egyptian airline Heliopolis, three MD90s and three options to KTHY Airlines of Turkey, one MD11 to Vasp Brazilian Airlines, and one MD11 to an unidentifed customer to be delivered in December.
The company has also completed negotiations with TWA for the sale of 13 of the MD80 family of aircraft, he said.
Ten of these are conversions of options announced in July for new MD83 aircraft.
The outstanding three aircraft are used MD82s, which will be delivered in December. The TWA deal is valued at $345 million.
